resources.name: Seal Web App API
resources.description:
Tested against a live server on 29 Aug 2026 with yt-dlp 2026.08.19, ffmpeg 9.0.1, curl_cffi 0.16.2.

Start the server first:  node server/index.js   (port 5000)

IMPORTANT: raise the request timeout in Insomnia (Preferences > General > Request Timeout) to at least 300000 ms. /api/resolve takes ~5 s on most platforms but ~106 s on YouTube, and the default timeout will abort it.

resources.name: 1 - Health
resources.description: Start here. Confirms the server is up without touching yt-dlp.

resources.name: Quality presets (health check)
resources.description:
NEEDS: nothing. No parameters, no body, no auth.

RETURNS: 200 with static preset lists.
{
  "video": [{ "value": "1080", "label": "Full HD (1080p)", "description": "..." }, ...8 items],
  "audio": [{ "value": "mp3", "label": "MP3", "description": "..." }, ...6 items]
}

SPEED: ~15 ms. No yt-dlp process is spawned, so this is the correct health check.

resources.name: 2 - Resolve + Stream (recommended)
resources.description: The two-step flow. /api/resolve says WHAT to download; /api/stream delivers it. Nothing is written to server disk.

resources.name: Resolve - Streamable (no merge)
resources.description:
NEEDS:
  url      (query, required) - any http(s) page URL yt-dlp supports
  quality  (query, optional) - max height in px, or 'best'. Default 360.

RETURNS 200:
{
  "title": "me irl",
  "extractor": "Streamable",
  "count": 1,
  "downloads": [{
    "filename": "me irl.mp4",
    "ext": "mp4",
    "needsMerge": false,
    "duration": 12,
    "url": "/api/stream?url=...&index=0&name=me%20irl.mp4"
  }]
}

KEY FIELDS:
  needsMerge=false -> single progressive file, native extension kept (.mp4/.mp3)
  needsMerge=true  -> video+audio merged by ffmpeg, extension becomes .mkv
  count            -> number of downloadable items. Always loop over downloads[].
  downloads[].url  -> relative path. Prefix with the base URL to fetch.

ERRORS:
  400 { "error": "Invalid URL format..." }        - url missing or not http(s)
  502 { "error": "Extraction failed", "details": "..." } - platform blocked or URL dead

SPEED: ~3-5 s typical. No media is transferred at this step.

resources.name: Resolve - Reddit (needs merge)
resources.description:
NEEDS: url, quality (same as above).

RETURNS 200 with needsMerge=true and ext=mkv:
{
  "title": "That small heart attack.",
  "extractor": "Reddit",
  "count": 1,
  "downloads": [{ "filename": "That small heart attack..mkv", "ext": "mkv", "needsMerge": true, ... }]
}

WHY IT DIFFERS: Reddit serves video and audio as two separate DASH streams. There is no single link to hand a browser, so the server merges them with ffmpeg. Extension becomes .mkv because MP4 cannot be written to a pipe (it needs to seek backwards to write its moov atom, and silently degrades to MPEG-TS).

VERIFIED: streaming this yields 1,961,387 bytes, matroska container, h264 + aac.

resources.name: Stream - download the file
resources.description:
NEEDS:
  url      (query, required) - same page URL passed to /api/resolve
  quality  (query, optional) - default 360
  name     (query, optional) - filename sent back in Content-Disposition
  index    (query, optional) - 0-based item for multi-video posts

RETURNS 200: the raw media bytes.
  Content-Type: application/octet-stream
  Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="me irl.mp4"; filename*=UTF-8''me%20irl.mp4

The filename* form carries non-ASCII titles correctly (real titles contain fullwidth quotes and similar).

IN INSOMNIA: the response pane shows binary. Use the download-response button to save it to a file.

DISK: nothing is written server-side. Verified downloads/ stayed at 0 items across a full stream.

CANCELLING: closing the request kills the yt-dlp process, so aborted downloads do not orphan processes.

ERRORS:
  400 plain text 'Invalid URL format.'
  502 empty body - extraction or merge failed (check server console)

VERIFY A MERGED FILE IS REAL (a corrupt merge still looks fine by byte count):
  ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=codec_name -of csv=p=0 out.mkv
  expect both h264 and aac; video-only means the merge failed.

resources.name: 3 - Resolve per platform
resources.description: Verified status per platform on 29 Aug 2026. Swap the url parameter to test others.

resources.name: YouTube - WORKS (slow, ~106 s)
resources.description:
STATUS: works. needsMerge=true, ext=mkv.
VERIFIED stream: 24,420,197 bytes, audio + video.

WARNING: resolve took 106 seconds. Raise the Insomnia timeout to 300000 ms or this looks like a hang.

WHY SLOW: yt-dlp must solve YouTube's player JS challenge. It is much slower still from a datacenter IP, where bot checks are aggressive - expect this to be the least reliable platform in production.

resources.name: Dailymotion - WORKS
resources.description:
STATUS: works.
VERIFIED stream: 37,626,318 bytes, audio + video.

NOTE: the raw platform URL is an .m3u8 playlist, not a video file. Handing that link to a browser saves a few KB of text. The server fetches and joins the segments, which is why the streamed result is a real file.

resources.name: BiliBili - WORKS (403 for browsers)
resources.description:
STATUS: works through the API.
VERIFIED stream: 2,191,613 bytes, audio + video.

WHY THE API IS REQUIRED HERE: BiliBili's CDN returns 403 to any request without a Referer header. A raw link is useless in a browser. yt-dlp sends the right header server-side, so routing through /api/stream is the only way this platform works at all.

resources.name: Instagram - WORKS
resources.description:
STATUS: works. needsMerge=false, ext=mp4.

NOTE ON count: the route passes --no-playlist, so a carousel post collapses to the first video and count=1. The underlying post exposes 3 separate videos; drop --no-playlist in stream.js if you want all of them, and count becomes 3.

Separately, GET /api/info returns 500 on this URL - see the Legacy folder.

resources.name: TikTok - FLAKY
resources.description:
STATUS: intermittent. Resolve succeeded (ext=mp4, needsMerge=false) but streaming failed twice with:
  ERROR: Unable to extract universal data for rehydration

yt-dlp solves a JS challenge that sometimes works and sometimes does not - two direct runs succeeded (2,748,647 bytes) while two API runs returned 0 bytes. Retry before concluding it is broken.

Requires curl_cffi, which is installed. Without it, TikTok fails immediately on TLS impersonation.

resources.name: Facebook - FAILS (needs login)
resources.description:
STATUS: fails.
  502 { "error": "Extraction failed", "details": "ERROR: [facebook] ...: Cannot parse data..." }

Logged-out scraping is blocked. This is the platform refusing, not a bug in the API. Fixing it requires passing session cookies (--cookies-from-browser), which is a real decision to weigh rather than a default.

Vimeo behaves similarly but differently: it resolves and streams 58 MB, yet the file contains audio only. yt-dlp reports 'Failed to parse XML: not well-formed' - an upstream extractor bug.

resources.name: 4 - Info
resources.description: Metadata endpoints. Slow, because each spawns yt-dlp.

resources.name: Video info
resources.description:
NEEDS: url (query, required).

RETURNS 200:
{ "id", "title", "description", "duration", "uploader", "upload_date", "view_count", "thumbnail", "webpage_url", "extractor",
  "formats": [{ "format_id", "ext", "quality", "filesize", "width", "height", "fps", "vcodec", "acodec", "format_note" }] }

SPEED: 5.1 s for Streamable, 45-85 s for YouTube.

KNOWN BUG: returns 500 on multi-video posts such as Instagram carousels -
  { "error": "Failed to parse video information", "details": "Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position 24016" }
Cause: --dump-json emits one JSON object per line, and info.js passes the whole buffer to a single JSON.parse. /api/resolve handles this correctly.

ERRORS: 400 if url is missing.

resources.name: Playlist info
resources.description:
NEEDS: url (query, required).

RETURNS 200: { "entries": [{ "id", "title", "url" }] }
The entry url is a direct CDN link and is often signed and short-lived, so do not store it.

SPEED: ~4 s.

resources.name: 5 - Legacy (disk-based)
resources.description: The original flow. Writes files to the server's downloads/ folder and never delivers them to the client. Superseded by Resolve + Stream.

resources.name: Start download (async)
resources.description:
NEEDS: JSON body.
  url       (required) - http(s) URL
  quality   (optional) - max height, e.g. "360"
  audioOnly (optional) - boolean
  format    (optional) - audio format when audioOnly is true

RETURNS 200 IMMEDIATELY (~20 ms):
  { "success": true, "downloadId": "1787841040153", "message": "Download started" }

This only confirms the process started. The file is NOT ready. Progress and completion are emitted over Socket.IO, which Insomnia cannot consume - poll 'List downloaded files' until the file appears.

CAUTION: no concurrency limit. Every call spawns another yt-dlp process (~54 MB each).

ERRORS: 400 { "error": "Invalid URL format..." }

resources.name: List downloaded files
resources.description:
NEEDS: nothing.

RETURNS 200: [{ "name": "me irl.mp4", "size": 3044857, "createdAt": "...", "modifiedAt": "..." }]
Empty array when downloads/ is empty.

Poll this after POST /api/download to detect completion.

resources.name: Delete a file
List formats (BROKEN)
resources.description:
NEEDS: url (query, required).

RETURNS 200 but always empty:
  { "video_formats": [], "audio_formats": [], "all_formats": [] }

CAUSE: the route parses the human-readable --list-formats table looking for a header containing 'format code' and 'extension' - the old youtube-dl header. Modern yt-dlp prints 'ID  EXT RESOLUTION | PROTO | VCODEC  ACODEC', so parsing never starts.

USE INSTEAD: GET /api/info, whose formats array is populated correctly.
